patches.value: Set r_j=2^(−(j+1)); this is a positive sequence decreasing to zero and every r_j≤1.
Set N_i=ceil(1/d_i) for each positive diameter d_i.

value.declaration: Define K_{iℓ} as the N_i equal closed subintervals of [0,1]; each length 1/N_i≤d_i.

patches.value: Let D=dim_H(E), F=E×[0,1]. First show 0≤D≤n<∞. Nonnegativity is part of the critical-exponent definition. If n=0, ℝ⁰ is a singleton and E is that singleton, so D=0. If n>0, compactness H002 implies boundedness: the open cover of E by radius-one balls has a finite subcover, so E lies in a bounded box. For every sufficiently small h>0, subdivide this box into at most C h^(−n) grid cubes, C independent of h, each of diameter ≤√n h. For every fixed real m>n the total m-power cost is at most C n^(m/2)h^(m−n), tending to zero. For any fixed scale δ>0, take h with √n h≤δ; this is a Nat-indexed δ-cover after appending empty sets, and its cost can be made arbitrarily small. Hence C_m(E,δ)=0 for every δ>0, so M008's exact supremum formula gives H^m(E)=0. Apply M012 at every NNReal exponent m>n to infer D≤m for every m>n; taking their infimum gives D≤n. Fix arbitrary q>D, so q>0. M003 at the NNReal coercion of q gives H^q(E)=0. Unfold M008: this is exactly the supremum over positive scales of the infimum of Nat-indexed cover costs, so every scale content C_q(E,r)=0. To ensure the admissible class at any r>0 is nonempty, cover E by open balls of radius r/3 and use compactness to extract a finite subcover; their diameters are ≤2r/3, and appending empty sets gives a Nat-indexed r-cover. Thus for every γ>0 the zero infimum supplies an r-cover of q-cost <γ. Set r_j=2^(−(j+1)) and γ_j=1/(j+1). For each j choose such an r_j-cover of cost <γ_j. Each nonempty zero-diameter member in Euclidean space is a singleton. Enumerate these by a finite or countable list and replace the k-th by an open ball containing it, of diameter ≤r_j and q-power cost <γ_j2^(−k−1); the total added cost is <γ_j. Leave positive-diameter members and empty members unchanged. The resulting cover has all nonempty diameters d_i positive, d_i≤r_j, and q-cost <2γ_j. For each i partition [0,1] into N_i=⌈1/d_i⌉ closed intervals of length 1/N_i≤d_i; since d_i≤1, N_i≤1/d_i+1≤2/d_i. The products U_i×K_iℓ cover F, have diameter ≤√2d_i, and form a countable family (a countable union of finite families), which can be enumerated by ℕ with empty sets appended. Their total (q+1)-cost is at most 2(√2)^(q+1)∑d_i^q<4(√2)^(q+1)γ_j, and their diameters are ≤√2r_j→0. For any δ>0, all sufficiently large j give admissible δ-covers of F, so C_(q+1)(F,δ)≤4(√2)^(q+1)γ_j; letting j→∞ gives zero content. Since this holds for every δ>0, M008's exact supremum formula gives H^(q+1)(F)=0. M012 at NNReal exponent q+1 gives dim_H(F)≤q+1. As this holds for every q>D, taking the infimum gives dim_H(F)≤D+1. For n=0, F is isometric to [0,1]; interval covers of mesh h have at most 1/h+1 members of diameter ≤h and total a-cost tending to zero for every a>1. Thus H^a(F)=0 for every a>1; M012 gives dim_H(F)≤a for each such a, and taking the infimum gives dim_H(F)≤1=D+1. Isometries preserve ediam, cover conditions and the exact M008 formula.
